comparison: Both evaluate TMEM16F TM4 mutations (C28-C34) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes position-dependent effects with experimental data from Figures 1b-f. Peer reviewers affirm these findings with 'high level of rigor' and note the demonstration of constitutive scramblase activity. OpenEval R3 also addresses C35-C36 which peer R1 includes, showing strong alignment on core TMEM16F findings.

Both evaluate TMEM16A TM4/6 mutations (C39-C43) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites Figures 3b-f showing position-dependent effects parallel to TMEM16F. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm lysine mutations in TMEM16A confer scramblase activity with 'high level of rigor.' OpenEval R7 addresses pharmacological validation (C44-C45) also covered in peer R2, showing complete agreement on TMEM16A findings.

Both evaluate OSCA1.2 mutations (C47-C52) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes PS exposure, G-V shifts, and kinetics from Figures 4b-g as key findings extending to OSCA family. Peer reviewers strongly support these as demonstrating OSCA conversion to scramblases with 'thorough characterization' and 'high level of rigor.' OpenEval R9-R10 address MD simulations and graded effects (C53-C57) also covered in peer R3.

Perfect alignment on OSCA1.2 stimulus-dependent scramblase activity (C58-C61). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites Figures 5a-c and 4f-g showing novel functional phenotype. Peer reviewers accept this as demonstrating stimulus-dependent activity with 'thorough characterization' and 'adequate evidence.'

Perfect alignment on TMEM63A findings (C65-C68). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes differential effects on PS exposure versus ion channel activity from Figures 6b-f. Peer reviewers confirm extension to mammalian OSCA/TMEM63 family with 'adequate evidence' and 'high level of rigor,' though noting breadth over depth as the strength.

Both evaluate central conclusions (C6-C7, C77-C78) but with different assessments. OpenEval rates C6-C7, C77 as SUPPORTED but notes C78 is speculative (overall SUPPORTED for R13). Peer reviewers rate all as SUPPORTED, with editor explicitly endorsing the evolutionary interpretation that proteins 'may have originally functioned as scramblases.' Peer review more accepting of speculative evolutionary claims.

Perfect alignment on mechanistic interpretation of hydropathy role (C69-C72). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes claims are supported by cited references and amino acid properties. Peer reviewers accept mechanism without challenge, with Reviewer 3 acknowledging it as interpretive but supported by 'compelling new evidence' about TM4/6 interface.

Perfect alignment on general design principle (C73-C76). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this as important general principle contextualizing findings within broader scramblase biology. Peer reviewers accept this as emerging from experimental data, with reviewers noting the 'conserved potential for both ion and lipid permeation.'

Both address TMC1 Beethoven mutation (C82-C83) but with different assessments. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C82 is supported by citation but C83 is explicitly speculative without direct experimental evidence. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the speculative connection as consistent with broader findings, with no reviewer challenging it.

OpenEval R1 addresses structural/evolutionary background (C1, C23-C24) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R10 covers extensive background claims (C1-C5, C18-C25, C86-C89) all rated SUPPORTED. Both treat these as established, uncontroversial foundational knowledge providing context. Peer review groups more background claims together.

OpenEval R2 addresses pre-study knowledge gaps (C2-C3, C25) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes these claims within broader background evaluation. Both accept these as accurately representing prior state of knowledge, establishing context for the study's novel findings.

OpenEval R19 addresses TMEM16 functional background (C9-C17) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R11 covers overlapping literature-based background including TMEM16 functions (C9-C17) plus additional claims, all rated SUPPORTED. Both treat these as established knowledge from citations, with peer review noting prior work from the same group.

OpenEval R20 addresses TMEM16 structure-function background (C18-C22, C26-C27) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes these within extensive background claims. Both accept these as established knowledge providing essential background for the study's findings.

OpenEval R21 addresses fundamental background (C4-C5, C86) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes these claims in broader background evaluation. Both treat as fundamental, uncontroversial background information.

OpenEval R22 addresses OSCA/TMEM63 background (C46, C62-C64, C87-C89) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R11 includes overlapping claims within literature-based background. Both accept these as established knowledge providing essential context for OSCA/TMEM63 family findings.

Both address evolutionary speculation (C78-C79) but with different assessments. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C78 is explicitly speculative requiring additional studies, though C79 has structural support. Peer R12 rates as SUPPORTED, accepting speculative interpretations as reasonable extensions, with Reviewer 3 acknowledging mechanism is 'still speculative' but evidence is strong.

Both address disease mutation speculation (C84-C85) but with different assessments. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C84 is supported by citation but C85 is explicitly speculative needing experimental validation. Peer R12 rates as SUPPORTED, accepting these as reasonable extensions of findings with acknowledgment that mechanism remains speculative.

OpenEval R4 addresses glutamate vs alanine substitution effects in TMEM16F (C35-C36) rated SUPPORTED based on Figure 1 supplement 2. Peer R1 includes these claims within broader TMEM16F evaluation, accepting differential substitution effects as part of the demonstration that charged residues destabilize the gate.

OpenEval R5 addresses TM6 mutations in TMEM16F (C37-C38) rated SUPPORTED based on Figures 2b-f. Peer R1 includes these claims in comprehensive TMEM16F evaluation, accepting extension from TM4 to TM6 as supporting the TM4/6 interface importance.

OpenEval R7 addresses pharmacological validation of TMEM16A mutant (C44-C45) rated SUPPORTED based on Figure 3 supplement 1. Peer R2 includes these claims within broader TMEM16A evaluation, accepting that mutant retains TMEM16A-specific inhibition sensitivity as part of rigorous characterization.

OpenEval R9 addresses MD simulation data for OSCA1.2 (C53-C54) rated SUPPORTED, noting simulations provide mechanistic insight though experimental validation would strengthen findings. Peer R3 includes these claims, describing MD simulations as adding 'supportive evidence' within the broader OSCA1.2 evaluation.

OpenEval R10 addresses graded effects of charged residue positioning in OSCA1.2 (C55-C57) rated SUPPORTED based on Figure 4 supplements and main figures. Peer R3 includes these claims within comprehensive OSCA1.2 evaluation, accepting graded effects as supporting the role of charged residue positioning.

OpenEval R23 addresses TMC1 background (C80) rated SUPPORTED based on cited reference. Peer R11 includes this claim within extensive literature-based background, accepting it as established knowledge providing context for Beethoven mutation discussion.
